business_problem: TBI needed distributed engineering and construction teams to collaborate quickly with the right BIM and graphics tools, but its users lacked a shared environment for large design files, simulation workloads, and partner-heavy projects that spanned dozens of organizations.
solution_summary: TBI built its BIM Cloud Workspace on Microsoft Azure using Azure NVads A10 v5 virtual machines, NVIDIA A10 Tensor Core GPUs, NVIDIA RTX Virtual Workstation, and NVIDIA Virtual GPU technology to give distributed construction teams a shared engineering environment. Project applications and desktops are published from Azure clusters so architects, designers, and analysts can access a controlled workspace with large BIM files on demand. GPU partitioning lets the IT team right-size compute and graphics profiles per user, from 4Q one-sixth-GPU slices to larger allocations, while Windows multi-session enables shared virtual workstation delivery. The stack supports game-engine tunnel simulations plus distribution of drone- and sensor-derived point clouds into 3D environments, so TBI can stress-test traffic, fire, and weather scenarios before assets are installed. This cloud VDI architecture replaced disconnected tool access with rapid provisioning and cheaper, workload-matched GPU allocation.
